fixed.problem: Blocking 1 (P7-12): the Overview's 'Change' and /settings#other-settings still did not land on Other settings. The reviewer measured the section 400 to 1900 px down a 900 px window. The hook scrolled once, smoothly, when Settings' rows loaded, then stopped watching. The sections above (models, subscription allowance, credential order, devices, sources, voice) load later and pushed the section down, and the smooth scroll aimed at where the section was when it began.
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/e2e/settings-links.spec.ts 'a link to Other settings lands on it after the sections above it load, and stops once the person scrolls' (new, Chromium: before, the section's top was 1158 px below the top of the scrolling area); apps/ui/test/polish-screens.test.tsx 'a section above that loads after the rows: it lands again, at once; once the person scrolls, it stops'
fixed.how: lib/use-hash-scroll.ts lands at once (scrollIntoView with behavior 'instant'). It lands again, throttled to one animation frame, whenever the page changes (MutationObserver on body for childList, subtree and characterData; ResizeObserver on body where it exists). It stops at the person's first wheel, touchstart, keydown, pointerdown or mousedown (capture listeners on window), or after 15 s, and the effect's cleanup stops it too. data-targeted is set once. The Inbox's #card- links use the same hook. In the Playwright spec the routes of the sections above are held back until the rows are visible. Once they load, the spec checks that the section's top is within 2 px of main's top. After a wheel scroll it checks that a later section (voice) no longer moves the page.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Fresh install (bench --fresh --provider bench, 1400x900 window). Open /settings#other-settings five times, and once more through an in-app navigation from Home. Each time, 'Other settings' is at the top of the page under the header. Bench before (sources put back to 3409c5b): fresh loads 352, 0, 0, 0, 0 px; in-app navigation 241, 385, 241 px. After: 0 px every time. On --provider bench-api --api-key refused, five fresh loads gave 0 px (the reviewer had 1387 to 1903). Scroll with the mouse wheel while the page still loads: it stays where you put it. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/fixup-polish-screens-evidence/bench1/03-before-in-app-link-top-241.png, 10-after-in-app-link-top-0.png, bench2/after2-hash-load-*-top-0.png. Live check (real model, githost or forerunner-sandbox project): on the Overview, click 'Merging: … · Change'. Settings opens with Advanced open and 'Other settings' at the top of the view.

fixed.how: shell/commands.ts: CommandContext gets viewedProjectId. The Start session entry names the project on screen with the hint 'the project on screen', else the active project with 'the active project'. That is the same choice Shell.tsx makes for the StartSessionDialog (viewed ?? activeProject). Shell passes viewed?.id and adds viewed to the memo's dependencies. The user guide and apps.md say the same.

fixed.problem: Non-blocking from the review (later #28): 'Save a new key' on 'Anthropic refused your API key' opens the setup assistant on its Claude step. That step said '✓ An API key is saved.' above 'Replace the API key'.
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/test/polish-screens.test.tsx 'there, the Claude step says the saved key was refused, never '✓ An API key is saved.'' (no setup-refused line)
fixed.how: SetupPage keeps which saved credential is refused (API key, subscription token), read from GET /settings/billing-order. Before, that read was used only to pick the first step. The Claude step then says 'Anthropic refused the saved API key. Paste a new one below.' (or the subscription token's sentence) in amber instead of '✓ … is saved.', until a new one of that kind passes its check. A refused subscription with no key saved opens the subscription tab. The test also saves a new key and checks that the line turns to 'An API key is saved.'
fixed.check_in_the_app: Bench --provider bench-api --api-key refused: run a task so the key is refused. Home's Needs you row offers 'Save a new key'. Click it: the setup assistant opens on Claude with Welcome ticked, and the amber line reads 'Anthropic refused the saved API key. Paste a new one below.' (/tmp/frbench/fixup-polish-screens-evidence/bench2/02-after2-setup-from-save-a-new-key.png). Paste a working key and click Check and save: the line becomes '✓ An API key is saved.'

not_done.problem: Opus fast mode's Settings row and card still quote 'USD 8 / 40 per million input / output tokens' (acceptance: no USD anywhere in Settings).
not_done.why: Unchanged from the fixer's not_done, and the reviewer marked it non-blocking for the session lead or owner to decide. It is the provider's price table (fastModeEffect in packages/runtime/src/models/fast-mode.ts, asserted by the commands fast-mode tests and ADR 0057). The user guide now names it as the one place USD remains, so it no longer claims 'CHF everywhere'. The new no-USD UI test excludes only the fast-mode card and the project.fast_mode rows.

not_done.problem: The subscription allowance's override line names the environment variable FORERUNNER_PLAN_USD_MONTHLY.
not_done.why: It is the exact name of a variable the person set and must remove; it is not an amount. It shows only when that variable decides the allowance.

not_done.problem: Other non-blocking review items: (1) the C-45 'each need more than the work budget' line names every task, with no 'and N more' after three; (2) the monthly cap's 0 refusal says why but not what to do, and through POST /commands/execute it reads only 'budget.set: invalid parameters'; (3) budget sentences use whole francs ('CHF 3'); (4) the handover change sentence repeats the schedule; (5) the Inbox's Yes explanation repeats a settings.set card's body (polish-words' request-words.ts); (6) the real-daemon 'opening a project writes nothing to GET /changes' case would also pass on the base; (7) palette.spec's row count (3409c5b) and the fake-daemon change it needs (eb1dfcc) are in different commits.
not_done.why: These are outside the three blocking findings. (1) to (4) are wording or command-text changes that touch commands tests or polish-words' shared sentences. (5) is polish-words' file. (6) adds no behaviour; the UI test carries the claim. (7) would need a history rewrite of the reviewed commits. Only the cheap UI items (the dialog after Start, the refused key on setup, the lint info) were done.
